sessions: ok so hola, Lucía (my novia, she's an architect, way more organized than me) said I should start using an assistant for my business stuff instead of 400 notes in my phone, so here I am. I'm Diego, I'm a wedding photographer in Guadalajara, I've been doing this like 8 years, before that I did product photos for a tequila brand which is funny because now half my weddings are in Tequila lol

first thing that's kind of urgent-ish. I have a big wedding on November 21st, Valeria and Andrés, at Hacienda Los Agaves in Tequila town. it's like 250 guests, super fancy, they want everything, drone, second shooter, album, the whole thing. the Valeria job is basically paying my rent until February so I want it perfect
my second shooter is Beto, we've worked together for years, he's great with the getting-ready shots and with the drunk uncles haha

the issue right now is the drone. the hacienda says I need a permit from them AND from the municipio because it's close to the agave fields that are UNESCO something something. I sent the forms two weeks ago and nada
do you know how drone rules work in Mexico in general? like do I need to register the drone with AFAC if it's under 2kg? mine is a Mini 4 Pro
ok so under 250g is basically chill, but the venue rules are still the venue rules. got it
oh and please, when you write stuff for me keep it relaxed, no "Estimado señor" corporate stuff, my clients are mostly millennials and I talk to them like friends, mitad español mitad inglés is fine

other thing! I'm also doing my own personal project, a photo book called "Mercados de Jalisco", markets all over the state, Tlaquepaque, San Juan de Dios, little pueblos. and there's going to be an exhibition at Galería Ocre, the curator is Renata Salas, opening February 2nd I think

the book is being printed by Andrés at Imprenta Fénix. different Andrés from the groom lol, Guadalajara has like a million Andréses. he needs my final files by December 15th for the book to be ready for the expo

can you help me write a short artist statement for the expo? like 120 words. it's about how markets are the last places where everyone in a city actually crosses paths, rich, poor, abuelitas, tourists, kids
me encanta. maybe less "poetic" in the last line, more direct
perfect perfect. ok gracias, Chispa (my dog) wants to go out
ok hi again, uploaded the Valeria contract from May so you have it. everything's in there
mala noticia. Beto broke his wrist playing fútbol on sunday. he's fine but in a cast for like 6 weeks so no Tequila wedding for him. 💀
so I called Karla Ibarra, she shot with me two times last year, she's really good with candids, and she said YES. so Karla is my second shooter for the 21st now. phew
also correction on the expo, Renata emailed, the opening at Galería Ocre is February 12th, not the 2nd. I had it wrong in my calendar. the 12th, a friday
which is actually better, more time to print. still need Andrés to have files by Dec 15 though

random question, Lucía and I are arguing, is it better to rent or buy a camera body for a one-off job? I'm thinking about upgrading anyway, either the Sony A7 IV or the Canon R6 Mark II, I literally can't decide, I've been going back and forth for a month. I shoot Sony now so lenses are a thing
ok the lens argument is strong for Sony but the R6 II autofocus for receptions... ugh. still not decided, I'll sleep on it for another month probably lol

also something to remember, from January I'm moving the studio from Colonia Americana to a bigger space in Chapultepec, Avenida Chapultepec near the Tuesday market. contract starts January 1st. right now still in Americana obviously
thanks amigo
YESSS the drone permit came through, both the hacienda and the municipio said ok, I got the papers yesterday. so drone is happening at the Tequila wedding

but now the new headache: Valeria still hasn't sent me the final timeline. like I don't know if the ceremony is at 5 or at 6, which matters a lot for golden hour portraits, and I can't plan the drone flight times or Karla's schedule without it. that's the thing stuck now
how do I ask her nicely for the timeline without sounding annoying? she's stressed with the wedding
jaja perfecto, very chill. I'll send that
also she asked if we could stay 12 hours instead of 10 because the after-party is going to be crazy. I said I'd check the contract
ok and question for my own planning, what's a good way to organize like 4,000 market photos for the book? I use Lightroom
color labels for "maybe/yes/hero" makes sense. ok
one more: what should I bring as a gift for Renata at the gallery, she's been super helpful. not alcohol, she doesn't drink
the book idea is lovely. ok bye
quick one. Lucía's asking when I'll finally be done with the Valeria editing because we want to go to Oaxaca in January. like what's my actual delivery deadline
ok cool, I'll tell her

also want to send Karla a message with the plan for the 21st: meet at the studio at 11am, drive together to Tequila, getting ready shots of Andrés with her, I do Valeria. can you write it? I'll send it on whatsapp
nice. thanks
random, what's the difference between ND filters and polarizers? a student asked me and I explained it badly
ahh yes ok that's clearer. byeee

documents.text:
CONTRATO DE SERVICIOS FOTOGRÁFICOS / PHOTOGRAPHY SERVICES AGREEMENT
Diego Morales Fotografía - Calle Libertad 1820, Col. Americana, Guadalajara, Jal.

CLIENTS: Valeria Ortega Lomelí and Andrés Cárdenas Ruiz
EVENT: Wedding - Saturday 21 November 2026
VENUE: Hacienda Los Agaves, Tequila, Jalisco

1. PACKAGE "Hacienda Completa" includes:
- Coverage by lead photographer and one second shooter for up to 10 continuous hours.
- Aerial photography with drone, subject to written permission from the venue and any applicable authority. If permission is not granted, the drone portion will be replaced by an additional 1 hour of ground coverage at no cost.
- Online gallery with a minimum of 600 edited images.
- One handmade lay-flat album 30x30 cm, 20 spreads, design included with up to 2 rounds of client revisions.

2. FEE. Total fee: MXN 48,000 (IVA included).

3. PAYMENT SCHEDULE.
- 30% (MXN 14,400) on signature, as a non-refundable reservation deposit.
- 40% (MXN 19,200) no later than 30 days before the event date.
- 30% (MXN 14,400) on delivery of the online gallery.

4. OVERTIME. Coverage beyond 10 hours is charged at MXN 3,500 per additional hour or fraction, per team (lead + second shooter).

5. DELIVERY. Edited images will be delivered via online gallery within eight (8) weeks after the event. The album will be delivered within six (6) weeks after the client approves the final design.

6. CANCELLATION. If the clients cancel more than 90 days before the event, the deposit is retained and no further amount is due. If they cancel within 90 days, 70% of the total fee is due.

7. MEALS. The clients will provide a hot meal for the photography team (2 people) during the reception.

8. USAGE. The photographer may use selected images for portfolio and social media unless the clients opt out in writing.

Signed in Guadalajara, 3 May 2026.
